level1.text: The source voltage of a battery is $1.58\,\text{V}$ and its internal resistance $0.25\,\Omega$. A current of $0.80\,\text{A}$ is drawn from the battery. What is the terminal voltage of the battery?

A rechargeable nickel-metal hydride cell has a source voltage of $1.30\,\text{V}$ and an internal resistance of $0.040\,\Omega$. What current would flow if the terminals of the cell were connected in a short circuit with a thick wire whose resistance is neglected?
A remote control has four batteries in series. The source voltage of each battery is $1.55\,\text{V}$. What is the source voltage of the group of batteries?
Three identical batteries are connected in parallel. The internal resistance of each battery is $0.45\,\Omega$. What is the internal resistance of the group of batteries?

The graph shows the measured points of the terminal voltage of a battery as a function of the current and a straight line drawn through them and extended to the axes. What is the short-circuit current of the battery? Read the value from the graph.

level2.text: Two different load resistors are connected to a battery in turn. With the first resistor the current is $0.20\,\text{A}$ and the terminal voltage $4.30\,\text{V}$, with the second the current is $0.80\,\text{A}$ and the terminal voltage $3.70\,\text{V}$. What is the internal resistance of the battery?

The source voltage of a voltage source is $6.0\,\text{V}$ and its internal resistance $0.50\,\Omega$. A resistor with a resistance of $5.5\,\Omega$ is connected to it. What is the terminal voltage of the source?

A torch lamp with a resistance of $3.0\,\Omega$ is connected to a battery whose source voltage is $4.5\,\text{V}$ and internal resistance $1.5\,\Omega$. The resistance of the lamp is assumed constant. What is the power of the lamp?

Two batteries are connected in series, and their load is a resistor of $2.4\,\Omega$. The source voltage of each battery is $1.5\,\text{V}$ and its internal resistance $0.30\,\Omega$. What current flows through the resistor?

level3.text: A camping lantern has two identical batteries in parallel so that the lantern works longer. The source voltage of each battery is $1.5\,\text{V}$ and its internal resistance $0.40\,\Omega$. The resistance of the lamp of the lantern is $0.80\,\Omega$, and it is assumed to stay constant. What current flows through each battery?

Three batteries are put into a torch in series, but one of them is put in the wrong way round by mistake. The source voltage of each battery is $1.5\,\text{V}$ and its internal resistance $0.25\,\Omega$. The resistance of the lamp is $4.0\,\Omega$, and it is assumed to stay constant. What current flows through the lamp?

A resistor of $2.0\,\Omega$ is first connected to a battery, and the terminal voltage of the battery is $1.20\,\text{V}$; then a resistor of $6.0\,\Omega$ is connected, and the terminal voltage is $1.44\,\text{V}$. The source voltage and the internal resistance of the battery are assumed to be the same in both measurements. What is the source voltage of the battery?
